issues.description: Define the RideNow system scope, microservice boundaries, API contracts, database ownership, and communication patterns. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, REST, PostgreSQL, Redis. AWS: EKS, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, API Gateway. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.summary: Define MVP scope and core ride flow
subtasks.description: Define Passenger and Driver flows: authentication, ride request, matching, acceptance, trip lifecycle, payment simulation, and history.
Define User, Driver, Trip, Matching, Payment, and Notification services. Assign clear responsibilities and avoid shared business logic.
Decide which operations use synchronous REST and which use asynchronous messaging. Tech: REST, SQS, EventBridge.
Define which service owns each database/table and prevent direct database access between services. Tech: PostgreSQL, database-per-service approach.
Design request/response models, endpoints, error formats, authentication requirements, and service-to-service APIs.
Document Frontend → API Gateway → EKS → Microservices → RDS/Redis and asynchronous flows through SQS/EventBridge.

issues.description: Implement user registration/login integration, user profiles, roles, and authorization. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, REST. AWS: Amazon Cognito, API Gateway, IAM. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create Spring Boot service responsible for user profile and user-related business logic.
Create User Pool, configure authentication, and obtain JWT tokens for authenticated users.
Validate Cognito JWTs and extract user identity and roles in the backend.
Implement role-based authorization so only permitted users can access Passenger or Driver operations.
Create APIs for retrieving and updating basic user information.

issues.description: Manage driver profiles, availability, online/offline state, and current location. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Redis. AWS: EKS, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create Spring Boot service responsible for driver-specific business logic.
Store driver information such as vehicle and basic profile data in PostgreSQL.
Allow drivers to become available or unavailable for ride matching and maintain consistent driver state.
Receive driver latitude/longitude updates and store active locations in Redis.
Use Redis GEO commands to store and query nearby available drivers.
Expire stale driver locations so disconnected or inactive drivers are not selected for matching.

issues.description: Manage the core ride lifecycle from request through completion. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, REST, transactions. AWS: EKS, RDS PostgreSQL. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create Spring Boot service responsible for ride/trip lifecycle and trip state.
Create PostgreSQL tables for rides/trips, passengers, drivers, locations, timestamps, status, and relevant indexes.
Allow passengers to request rides with pickup and destination information.
Define valid states such as REQUESTED, MATCHED, ACCEPTED, ARRIVING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED.
Implement driver/passenger operations for accepting, arriving, starting, completing, and cancelling trips.
Provide paginated ride history APIs with appropriate PostgreSQL indexes.
Use Spring transactions to keep critical trip state changes consistent.

issues.description: Find and select suitable nearby drivers for requested rides. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, Redis GEO, REST. AWS: EKS, ElastiCache Redis. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create Spring Boot service responsible for driver discovery and matching logic.
Use Redis GEOSEARCH to find available drivers within a configured radius.
Rank candidates using simple factors such as distance and driver availability.
Temporarily reserve a driver while the ride request is being offered to prevent conflicting assignments.
Release failed or expired matching attempts and try another candidate when appropriate.
Return a clear result when no suitable available driver exists.

issues.description: Prevent race conditions when multiple drivers attempt to accept the same ride. Tech: PostgreSQL transactions, row locking, optimistic locking, Redis atomic operations. AWS: RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Identify race-prone operations such as multiple drivers accepting one ride and multiple requests modifying driver state.
Use PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE where appropriate to serialize critical ride updates.
Use a version field with JPA @Version for entities where optimistic concurrency is appropriate.
Ensure only one driver can successfully claim a requested ride even under concurrent requests.
Prevent duplicate processing when clients retry ride acceptance, payment, or other critical requests.
Send concurrent requests and verify that only one driver wins the acceptance race.

issues.description: Implement simulated payment processing after trip completion. Tech: Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, transactions, idempotency. AWS: EKS, RDS PostgreSQL. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create Spring Boot service responsible for simulated payment processing.
Store payment status, trip ID, amount, transaction ID, and timestamps.
Create a fake payment provider and simulate successful and failed payment scenarios.
Ensure retrying the same payment request does not create duplicate transactions.
Handle temporary failures safely without creating duplicate payments.

issues.description: Move independent background operations to asynchronous processing. Tech: SQS, DLQ, workers, EventBridge. AWS: Amazon SQS, EventBridge, EKS. Priority: SHOULD HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create queues for background jobs such as notifications or other retryable operations.
Configure DLQ and max receive count for messages that repeatedly fail.
Create a worker that consumes SQS messages and processes notifications asynchronously.
Handle temporary failures and allow SQS to retry failed messages.
Publish events such as TripCompleted or PaymentCompleted using EventBridge.
Create consumers for selected business events without tightly coupling services.

issues.description: Handle multi-service workflows where one database transaction cannot cover the entire operation. Tech: EventBridge, service events, compensation, eventual consistency. AWS: EventBridge. Priority: SHOULD HAVE.

subtasks.description: Identify operations that span Trip, Payment, Driver, and Notification services.
Define how TripCompleted triggers payment and other independent operations.
Document which data may temporarily differ between services and how it becomes consistent.
Define simple compensation actions when a downstream operation fails.

issues.description: Provide live trip and driver location updates. Tech: WebSocket, Redis Pub/Sub, Spring WebSocket. AWS: EKS, ElastiCache Redis. Priority: SHOULD HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create WebSocket connections for passengers and drivers to receive real-time updates.
Use Redis Pub/Sub to distribute real-time events between service instances.
Publish driver location updates to the appropriate trip/passenger channel.
Push ride state changes such as ACCEPTED, ARRIVING, IN_PROGRESS, and COMPLETED.

issues.description: Deploy and operate RideNow microservices on Kubernetes. Tech: Kubernetes, Docker, YAML, kubectl. AWS: Amazon EKS, ECR, ALB. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Create the Kubernetes cluster and worker capacity required for RideNow services.
Organize RideNow workloads using appropriate namespaces.
Create Deployments for each Spring Boot microservice.
Expose internal microservices using Kubernetes Services.
Route external API traffic to the appropriate services using AWS Load Balancer Controller and ALB.
Add health endpoints and Kubernetes probes so unhealthy containers are removed or restarted.
Define CPU and memory requests/limits for services.
Configure HPA for selected services and test scaling behavior under load.

issues.description: Build the AWS infrastructure required to run RideNow securely. AWS: VPC, private subnets, security groups, EKS, RDS, ElastiCache, ECR, API Gateway, Secrets Manager, IAM. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Design VPC CIDR, public/private subnets, routing, and availability zones for the application.
Allow only required traffic between ALB, EKS, RDS, Redis, and other AWS resources.
Create PostgreSQL database infrastructure with appropriate networking and security.
Create Redis infrastructure for GEO data, temporary state, locking where justified, and Pub/Sub.
Create ECR repositories for each microservice Docker image.
Store database credentials, API secrets, and other sensitive configuration securely.
Create least-privilege IAM permissions required by EKS workloads and AWS services.
Expose the RideNow API entry point and configure authentication, throttling, and routing as required.

issues.description: Define AWS infrastructure and Kubernetes-related infrastructure using code. Tech: Terraform or CloudFormation. AWS: VPC, EKS, RDS, ElastiCache, ECR, IAM, Secrets Manager. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Select Terraform or CloudFormation and define project structure.
Create VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT, security groups, and related resources through IaC.
Define EKS, ECR, RDS, Redis, IAM, Secrets Manager, and other required resources.
Separate configuration for development and production environments where appropriate.
Deploy infrastructure from a clean environment and verify that resources are reproducible.

issues.description: Automate building, testing, publishing, and deploying RideNow services. Tech: GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes. AWS: ECR, EKS, CloudWatch. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Use short-lived feature branches, pull requests, code review, and protected main branch.
Create production-ready Docker images for each Spring Boot service.
Run compilation, unit tests, and basic validation automatically on pull requests.
Build Docker images and push versioned images to Amazon ECR.
Automatically update Kubernetes Deployments with the new image version.
Integrate Flyway or Liquibase migrations into the deployment process.
Verify that failed deployments can be rolled back to the previous working version.

issues.description: Validate correctness, integration, concurrency, reliability, and system behavior. Tech: JUnit 5, Mockito, REST Assured, Testcontainers, WireMock, k6. AWS: LocalStack/AWS test environment. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Test service business logic and domain rules using JUnit 5 and Mockito.
Test REST endpoints, validation, authentication, authorization, and error responses.
Use Testcontainers PostgreSQL to test real database behavior, transactions, and constraints.
Test communication between microservices using real or mocked dependencies.
Test SQS message processing, retries, failures, and DLQ behavior.
Send simultaneous ride acceptance requests and verify locking and consistency.
Test the complete Passenger and Driver ride flow from authentication to trip completion.
Use k6 to test API throughput, latency, concurrent ride requests, and selected high-load endpoints.
Test service failures, pod restarts, message failures, retries, and recovery behavior.

issues.description: Build a lightweight frontend focused on validating the backend rather than UI polish. Tech: Flutter, Dart, REST, WebSocket. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Implement login/register flow and Cognito authentication.
Allow passengers to enter pickup/destination and request a ride.
Display driver information, trip status, and basic trip information.
Allow drivers to go online/offline, receive ride requests, and manage trip states.
Send simulated or device-based driver location updates to the backend.
Display WebSocket-based trip and location updates if real-time tracking is implemented.
Display completed/cancelled rides using backend pagination APIs.

issues.description: Monitor application health, logs, metrics, and deployment behavior. AWS: CloudWatch, EKS Container Insights where appropriate. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Collect Spring Boot container logs in CloudWatch.
Implement Spring Boot Actuator health endpoints for Kubernetes probes.
Monitor request rate, latency, errors, CPU, memory, pod health, and relevant business metrics.
Create alarms for important failures such as high error rates or unhealthy infrastructure.
Create a simple CloudWatch dashboard for application and infrastructure health.
Document what is logged, monitored, alerted, and how engineers investigate failures.

issues.description: Apply basic production-oriented security and resilience practices. Tech: JWT, IAM, validation, rate limiting, retries, timeouts. AWS: Cognito, IAM, Secrets Manager, API Gateway, Security Groups. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Validate request data and reject malformed or invalid input.
Ensure users can only access resources and operations permitted by their role.
Store credentials and sensitive configuration in AWS Secrets Manager instead of source code or Docker images.
Grant AWS permissions only to the resources and actions required by each workload.
Protect public APIs using API Gateway throttling and appropriate application-level controls.
Configure reasonable timeouts and controlled retries for service-to-service communication.
Return meaningful errors and prevent cascading failures when dependencies are unavailable.

issues.description: Document the architecture, APIs, deployment, testing, and technical decisions and prepare the final demonstration. Priority: MUST HAVE.

subtasks.description: Document microservices, AWS infrastructure, data flow, and communication patterns.
Document REST APIs, request/response models, authentication, and error handling.
Document service database ownership, schemas, important indexes, and consistency decisions.
Document IaC deployment, Docker image flow, CI/CD pipeline, and EKS deployment.
Document unit, integration, API, concurrency, E2E, load, and failure testing.
Demonstrate the complete ride flow, concurrent acceptance, Redis matching, asynchronous processing, Kubernetes deployment, and observability.

issues.description: Implement additional features only after all MUST HAVE and important SHOULD HAVE work is stable. Tech/AWS depends on selected feature. Priority: OPTIONAL.

subtasks.description: Allow passengers and drivers to rate each other after completed trips.
Add dedicated metrics collection and dashboards if the team has sufficient time.
Experiment with advanced deployment strategies after reliable rolling deployments are complete.
Introduce additional caching only where profiling shows a real performance benefit.
Improve visual design and animations only after backend and DevOps requirements are complete.
